 Football
 Soccer-Odegaard seals narrow win for Arsenal, Man City lose again
 By Martyn Herman 
 Saturday, 07 Nov 2026
 | 10:54 PM MYT
 share 
 bookmark 
 Soccer Football - Premier League - Leeds United v Tottenham Hotspur - Elland Road, Leeds, Britain - November 7, 2026 Leeds United's Noah Okafor celebrates scoring their first goal REUTERS/Scott Heppell 
 LONDON, England, Nov 7 (Reuters) - Arsenal banked another three ⁠points in their Premier League title defence as their trademark persistence paid off in a 1-0 home win over stubborn Hull City but Manchester City ⁠suffered a third successive league defeat, 3-1 at Nottingham Forest on Saturday.
 It was not fluent or convincing but Martin Odegaard's poacher's goal in the ‌72nd-minute earned Mikel Arteta's Arsenal side a sixth league win by a single-goal margin this season.
 City's early-season flourish is now a fading memory as they head into the international break six points behind Arsenal.
 Enzo Maresca's side were two down inside 20 minutes at the City Ground as goals by Jair Cunha and Liam Delap lit the fuse for a Forest side who began the day 19th after taking one point ​from their last five games.
 Rayan Cherki halved the deficit early in the second half but Forest weathered ⁠the storm and Delap broke away to smash his second goal ⁠of the game to spark delirium inside the stadium.
 Arsenal have 27 points from 10 games, six clear of City whose defeat left neighbours Manchester United in the relegation ⁠zone ‌ahead of their Sunday clash with Aston Villa.
 Brighton & Hove Albion could cut Arsenal's lead to five points if they beat Brentford on Sunday.
 Arsenal showed last season a champions knack for picking up wins without hitting top gear as they claimed the title for the first time in 22 years and it was very much ⁠in evidence against a Hull side who provided a stiff test.
 Captain Odegaard had not scored since ​September but was on hand to snaffle a rebound ‌after Noni Madueke's shot had been saved by Hull keeper Konstantinos Tzolakis.
 They have now equalled their best ever start to a Premier League campaign after ⁠10 matches, although manager Mikel ​Arteta would prefer wider winning margins.
 "We need to find ways to be more efficient, sometimes even more pragmatic," the Spaniard said.
 "We need to be much more chaotic than that, and that's it. And score much earlier because obviously that's going to change the course of the game."
 ON-PITCH STRUGGLES
 Whatever fate awaits City after being found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges in relation to breaking ⁠Premier league financial rules -- charges they strongly deny -- the fact is they are struggling on the ​pitch.
 The fragility that seeped in during Pep Guardiola's final season in charge at the Etihad Stadium has continued and it was evident against Forest in a dismal first-half display.
 Jair Cunha punished sloppy defending after six minutes and Delap powered through to make it 2-0 with a fine finish past Gianluigi Donnarumma.
 Cherki's thunderbolt seemed to have given City a lifeline but ⁠Delap finished them off in style with a rasping shot from an angle that cannoned in off the post.
 Forest moved up to 16th place with nine points, leaving Manchester United in 18th on seven.
 Resurgent Tottenham Hotspur were seeking a fourth successive league win but substitute Noah Okafor drove home a low shot from the edge of the area in the 79th minute to give Leeds United a deserved 1-0 victory at Elland Road.
 It ended a five-match winless league run for Leeds and moved them above Tottenham into ​eighth place with 14 points.
 The big talking point, though, was Leeds's Jaden Bogle avoiding a red card for his rash ⁠lunge on Mathys Tel which resulted in the Tottenham winger being forced off with an ankle injury -- the VAR check on the challenge taking four minutes.
 Visiting manager Roberto de Zerbi, ​however, played down the controversy.
 "I'm sorry for the result, but first of all I'm sorry for the performance ‌in the second half," the Italian said. "We didn't play like a top team, we ​played without the right spirit, the right character, the right physicality in the duels."
 Fulham and Newcastle United shared the spoils in a 1-1 draw at Craven Cottage, Jacob Murphy giving the hosts a late lead only for Rodrigo Muniz to equalise.
 (Reporting by Martyn Herman; editing by Clare Fallon and Ed Osmond)
